title: Handoff Artifacts
description: Typed handoff contracts between workflow stages. Each stage with a `produces` field writes .work-state/artifacts/<id>.json matching the schema below. Downstream stages declare these ids in `consumes` and read them from disk instead of receiving pasted prose. Artifacts survive context compaction and make the inter-stage contract explicit.

answers.description: User answers (interactive) or auto-resolved defaults with rationale (autonomous).

chosen.description: Option id chosen by user (interactive) or option #1 (autonomous).

api_contract.description: DTOs/endpoints shared by backend+frontend in full-stack tasks.

scope.description: Project-defined scope names touched (e.g. backend-kotlin, go, frontend, mobile, devops, rust). Matches scope_map in team.config.

verdict.description: Normalized overall verdict, derived DETERMINISTICALLY from findings (not eyeballed): `reject` if any unresolved CRITICAL finding; else `needs_changes` if any HIGH or MEDIUM; else `approve`. The review stage gate keys on this (`verdict != reject`) instead of a subjective 'confidence>=80'. An unknown/missing verdict blocks closure — it never auto-approves.

zone.description: Project-defined scope name (e.g. backend-kotlin, go, frontend, mobile, devops, rust) matching a scope_map entry. Used to route the Phase 6.5 fix to the right developer role.

findings.description: Only findings with confidence >= 80 are recorded.

manual_qa.description: Manual runtime-verification verdict, produced by the manual-qa agent AFTER review_fixes — it exercises the code that will actually ship, not a pre-fix snapshot. NOT UI-only: on a UI scope it drives the real UI through OMP browser or configured device automation; on a backend/CLI scope it runs the app, hits endpoints, and reads logs/output. Gated on scope.has_runtime (skipped only for pure docs/config work). Consumed by qa_tests (evidence → automated regression tests) and by summary. Replaces the old string field inside `debug`.

verdict.description: PASS only if every acceptance criterion was observed working at runtime. A missing/unknown verdict is treated as FAIL — it never auto-passes.

evidence.description: Concrete observations. UI: screenshot path + WHAT IS VISIBLE on it. Backend/CLI: the command/curl run + the actual response/exit code, and the relevant log lines. A bare 'looks good' is not evidence.

mode.description: Which verification mode was used: 'ui' (OMP browser for web or configured device automation for the app) when scope.has_ui, else 'runtime' (run/curl/logs).

dod_additions.description: UI/visual acceptance criteria manual-qa appends back to dod.json (see multi-source DoD fan-in). Each item uses the dod item shape.

regressions.description: Pre-existing behavior that broke during testing — empty array if none.

qa_tests.description: Automated tests written by the qa agent AFTER manual_qa, encoding the manually-observed behavior (manual_qa.evidence) as durable regression tests. Only accepted when manual_qa.verdict == PASS, or when the task has no UI (!scope.has_ui) so manual_qa was skipped.

based_on_manual_qa.description: true when the tests encode manual_qa observations (has_ui path).

feature_spec.description: Optional slim feature specification — 8 sections distilled from a 15-section template. The discovery stage of a FEATURE workflow MAY produce it when the task warrants a written contract; it is not mandatory. Consumed by architecture and by manual-qa (acceptance_criteria becomes the manual test checklist). Gate-able via feature_spec_present when a project wants to require it.

goal.description: One-paragraph statement of what and why.

anti_scope.description: Explicitly out of scope — the boundary.

acceptance_criteria.description: Observable pass/fail criteria; manual-qa consumes these directly as its checklist.

testing_strategy.description: How the feature will be tested (manual + automated).

product_intake.description: Normalized product discovery intake: what the request is, what is known, and what is not. Evidence-first — every claim carries a verified|assumption|unknown status with its source, and explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' is an allowed answer but must never be guessed. The intake is produced by a parallel consilium (product-analyst + product-researcher), so every content field is a MERGEABLE ARRAY: strict fan-in concatenates the slots' arrays deterministically, and a single scalar (problem_statement/context) would block on the first divergent phrasing between the two roles. Empty arrays are valid; 'unknown'/'TBD' string entries are the explicit way to represent missing knowledge.

problem_statements.description: The product problem or opportunity, one or two sentences per entry, from each intake role; 'TBD' allowed only when genuinely unknown and marked as such.

contexts.description: Business/product context per intake role; explicit 'unknown' entries allowed.

stakeholders.description: Stakeholders affected by or interested in the problem; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

constraints.description: Constraints that bound any solution; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

open_questions.description: Open questions that must be answered before the direction is decided; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

status.description: verified = observed/confirmed from a source; assumption = unverified but stated as such; unknown = not known yet.

source.description: Where the claim came from (file:line, interview, doc, web source); 'n/a' for explicit assumptions/unknowns.

product_framing.description: Problem framing produced by the product analyst from the intake: restated problem, target users, success criteria and non-goals. Verified facts and assumptions stay distinct.

target_users.description: Who experiences the problem; 'unknown'/'TBD' allowed explicitly.

success_criteria.description: Observable product outcomes that would show the problem is solved.

non_goals.description: Explicitly out of scope for this discovery.

assumptions.description: Assumptions shaping the framing, each marked as an assumption (never dressed as a verified fact).

product_evidence.description: Evidence and alternatives gathered by the product researcher: verified facts, assumptions, unknowns, evidence gaps, and product alternatives considered. No fabricated data or invented sources.

status.description: verified = observed/confirmed; assumption = unverified but stated; unknown = not known yet.

source.description: Where the claim came from (file:line, doc, web source, interview); 'n/a' for explicit assumptions/unknowns.

gaps.description: Evidence gaps that must be validated before the direction can be considered solid.

product_critique.description: Adversarial review of the framing and evidence. The verdict is one of proceed|needs_more_validation|defer|reject and is never softened to be agreeable.

verdict.description: proceed = evidence supports moving to approval; needs_more_validation = direction plausible but evidence insufficient; defer = right area, not now; reject = the framing/direction itself is wrong or unsafe.

findings.description: Concrete critique points: unsupported claims, weak evidence, missing alternatives, framing errors.

blocking_gaps.description: Evidence or analysis gaps that must close before proceed.

product_spec.description: Synthesized product direction prepared by the product strategist from framing, evidence and critique. Product-level only — no APIs, no architecture, no implementation details. Every product-level concept is REQUIRED as its own field: an unknown/TBD concept is represented by an explicit array entry (e.g. 'unknown'/'TBD') or the string 'unknown', never by silently omitting the field — a spec that only carries recommendation/value/risk is not a decision.

recommendation.description: The strategist's recommendation to the product owner.

value_proposition.description: What is delivered, to whom, and why it matters; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

opportunity.description: Size/attractiveness of the opportunity; 'unknown' allowed explicitly.

target_users.description: Who the direction is for; explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' entries allowed.

solution_direction.description: Product-level direction (what and why) — deliberately NOT an implementation plan; 'TBD' allowed explicitly.

success_metrics.description: Observable product outcomes that would show the direction works; explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' entries allowed.

guardrail_metrics.description: Metrics that must NOT regress (safety/constraints the direction may not trade away); explicit 'unknown'/'TBD' entries allowed.

scope.description: What the direction covers; explicit 'TBD' entries allowed.

anti_scope.description: Explicitly out of scope — the boundary that stops creep; explicit 'TBD' entries allowed.

risks.description: Risks that remain even after critique; explicit 'unknown' entries allowed.

validation_plan.description: What must be validated before/after implementation; empty when recommendation is proceed.

evidence_trace.description: Maps each recommendation claim to product_evidence items by verified|assumption|unknown status.

open_decisions.description: Product decisions still open for the owner; empty when none.

product_prd.description: Deterministic Markdown product PRD rendered by the engine from the five product-discovery source artifacts. Exact manifest fields — no extras, none missing. content is the rendered markdown; content_hash is sha256 of it and of the document file bytes; source_hash is the deterministic key-order-independent hash of the five source artifacts at render time (stale sources are detected by re-hashing).

path.description: Safe relative path of the markdown document inside the state dir.

source_artifacts.description: The five source artifact ids in fixed order.

source_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical serialization of the five source artifacts at render time.

content.description: The full rendered markdown; must equal the document file bytes.

product_approval_record.description: Durable record of the human product-owner approval. Interactive only — product approval is never auto-approved or inferred; the decision must be exactly one of proceed|needs_more_validation|defer|reject, recorded via workflow_checkpoint with mode=interactive.

approved_by.description: Who approved — always a human product owner, never an autonomous agent.

product_handoff.description: Handoff of an approved product direction to the next workflow. next_workflow is 'spec-preparation' ONLY when decision == 'proceed'; for needs_more_validation | defer | reject it MUST be 'none' with a blocked_reason.

product_spec_artifact.description: Artifact id of the approved product spec (e.g. 'product_spec').

instructions.description: What the next workflow must spec and what evidence it must preserve.

blocked_reason.description: Why the direction was NOT handed off; required when decision != proceed.

dod.description: Definition of Done — acceptance criteria fixed BEFORE code, each with how it is verified and (when closed) the proof. Produced early (clarify/discovery/diagnose), then FANNED IN by later stages: every role with relevant context may APPEND items (with source + unique id) or CLOSE an existing item (pending→met with evidence). The dod_complete gate and the Stop backstop (hooks/dod-gate.sh) require every item met WITH evidence before a task may claim done.

id.description: Unique item id, convention `<source>-<n>` (e.g. architecture-1). Lets fan-in contributors append without colliding and lets closers reference a specific item.

source.description: Stage id that contributed this item (e.g. exploration, architecture, code_review, qa_tests, manual_qa). Defaults to the producing stage.

criterion.description: Concrete, observable acceptance criterion — not 'works' but what specifically must happen.

verify_method.description: How it is checked: a manual-qa scenario, a screenshot that must show X, a test, a curl.

evidence.description: Proof: gist URL, screenshot path + WHAT IS VISIBLE on it (input/output present? errors?), test output, curl result, root-cause statement. A bare checkbox is not proof.

contributions.description: Optional audit trail of the fan-in: keyed by contributing stage id. The interpreter/hooks never require it, but it makes the multi-source history inspectable.

closed.description: Item ids this stage moved pending→met.

by.description: Agent name(s) that made the contribution.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last append/close. Bumped on every fan-in write.

type_requirements_met.description: Confirms the per-type minimum items are present. Minimums: BUG_FIX → root cause named (not symptom) + repro-before reproduces + repro-after does not + affected scenario checked in manual-qa. FEATURE → each acceptance criterion mapped to a manual-qa step (both remote+docker modes if the feature touches agent/sessions). QA/report → published via publish-gist-report skill, screenshots actually visible (not broken). Any UI → DoD records what must be visible on the screenshot; on close, what is actually visible is written.

teams_hint.description: Team ids the CTO already considers relevant (optional, from scope analysis).

summary.description: Compact lead summary — raw artifacts stay in .work-state/artifacts/<team>/.
